solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One who's out and about

parts.note: reads as a busy sociable person, but describes someone roaming while 'out' in the sense of fast asleep

explanation.definitionFit: A person who wanders around while asleep is literally out cold yet up and about.

clue.text: Visit park and refuse to leave

parts.note: to visit somewhere is to stay there for a while
to park something is to put it down somewhere

explanation.surface: Someone visiting a park digs in and won't go home.
explanation.definitionFit: Stubbornly remaining where you are is an idiom for declining to move or go.

clue.text: We hear forty of the Romans do better

indicators.note: signals that the letters are judged by how they are spoken aloud

parts.note: forty in Roman numerals is XL

explanation.surface: Listeners are told some forty Romans will outperform others.
explanation.walkthrough: Say the Roman numeral XL out loud as letters and it sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To excel is a synonym for outperforming, surpassing or being superior.

clue.text: Puts order into projects

indicators.note: the words are turned into something new, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: An instruction to impose some discipline on a set of plans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'projects' looks like a noun (plans), but it is a verb: sticks out. The letters of PUTS ORDER are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that projects juts out beyond its surroundings, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Doctor on morning rounds

indicators.note: one piece is placed on, following, the other

parts.note: AM is the abbreviation for morning, ante meridiem
MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: A GP making the morning ward rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rounds' suggests a doctor's visits but means rounds of ammunition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rounds are cartridges or bullets, and ammunition is the collective term for them.

clue.text: Jumper with a pocket

parts.note: suggests a sweater with a pouch, but describes a leaping marsupial with a pouch

explanation.definitionFit: This Australian marsupial bounds along and carries its young in a pouch.

clue.text: Check the advance of a sick man getting up

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a leper is a man sick with leprosy

explanation.surface: Stopping an ill man from rising out of bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To repel an enemy is to drive back or halt their advance.

clue.text: Hard stone field used for playing baseball

definitions.meaning: the infield of a baseball ground is shaped like a square on its point

explanation.surface: A gem and the playing area of a ballgame.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the precious stone and the infield of a baseball park.

clue.text: Garage worker tuned machine to go over a hundred

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sits over, above, the next
an engine that is tuned is adjusted and reset, so the letters are reset

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A garage hand tunes an engine until it revs past a hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tuned' fits the garage surface but signals the rearrangement; 'to go over' places the scrambled word above C in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A mechanic is the tradesman who repairs vehicles in a garage.

clue.text: He always ends up in the relay race or tug-of-war

definitions.text: He always ends up in the relay race or tug-of-war

parts.words: He always ends up in the relay race or tug-of-war
parts.note: the person who runs the final leg of a relay or holds the back of a tug-of-war rope

explanation.definitionFit: The last runner of a relay team and the back puller in tug-of-war both carry this title.

clue.text: Religious representation of two Greek letters

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
eta is another Greek letter

explanation.surface: A holy image labelled with two letters of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A pietà is a painting or sculpture of Mary holding the dead Christ.

clue.text: Worthless friend put to the test

parts.note: a pal is a friend
to try something is to test it

explanation.surface: Testing whether a supposed friend is any good.
explanation.definitionFit: Paltry means trifling or of little value, a near synonym.

clue.text: Oh boy! All round publicity!

indicators.note: the letters are turned round into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An excited exclamation about a media frenzy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballyhoo is noisy, extravagant promotion or fuss, which is publicity.

clue.text: Stream of invective I get in traffic

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: traffic in goods is trade

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in a jam lets rip with abuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'traffic' suggests road congestion but means commerce.
explanation.definitionFit: A tirade is a long angry speech, a torrent of abuse.

clue.text: Shaped up again — to a more moral life?

definitions.meaning: formed once more, given a shape again
describes a person who has mended their ways

explanation.surface: Someone got back in shape and also changed their ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Re-formed means shaped anew, and reformed means having turned to better behaviour.

clue.text: Joined in, without being searched

indicators.note: in the old sense outside, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: an area that is combed has been searched thoroughly

explanation.surface: Someone joined a group without having been frisked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here has its old meaning, outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Combined means united or joined together, a synonym.

clue.text: Sleeping partner?

parts.note: in business a silent investor, but literally someone sharing your bed

explanation.definitionFit: This is someone you share a bed with, figuratively an associate.

clue.text: Fish thrash around wildly

explanation.surface: A landed fish flapping about on the deck.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a flatfish and a verb for struggling helplessly.

clue.text: Denials of faults in the show ring

definitions.meaning: in showjumping a horse balking at a fence incurs faults

explanation.surface: A show-jumping judge rejecting appeals over penalty points.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means turning down requests and also a horse balking at a jump.

clue.text: Royal train, perhaps?

parts.note: suggests a railway train, but means the procession of attendants following a monarch

explanation.definitionFit: A retinue is the group of attendants accompanying an important person, a train of followers.

clue.text: Orders to back team put around court

indicators.note: one piece is wrapped round the other

parts.note: a side is a team

explanation.surface: A coach's instructions for the team to support each other on court.
explanation.walkthrough: EDIS, from 'team' turned by 'to back', goes around CT.
explanation.definitionFit: Edicts are official decrees or commands, which are orders.

clue.text: A help or a hindrance in the works

definitions.text: A help or a hindrance in the works

parts.words: A help or a hindrance in the works
parts.note: a workshop tool that helps, yet thrown 'in the works' it sabotages

explanation.definitionFit: This tool aids mechanics, and the idiom about throwing one in the works means causing disruption.

clue.text: Point finally reached after weeks of study in America

parts.note: a term is a period of weeks in the academic year
US is the United States

explanation.surface: A student's arrival at the end of a semester abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A terminus is the end point, especially the last stop of a line.

clue.text: Schemes thrown aside

indicators.note: thrown into disorder, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Plans that have been discarded.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideas are plans or proposals, so schemes is a synonym.

clue.text: Girl carries on in Juliet's place

indicators.note: one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: Vera is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl soldiering on in the role of Shakespeare's Juliet.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare set the story of Romeo and Juliet in this Italian city.

clue.text: Ready to start acting from the beginning

definitions.meaning: an actor waiting on the film set

explanation.surface: An actor waiting for the cameras to roll.
explanation.definitionFit: On set describes an actor ready to perform, and onset means the start.

clue.text: One in the front row when the game starts

definitions.text: One in the front row when the game starts

parts.words: One in the front row when the game starts
parts.note: suggests a spectator, but means a chess piece lined up in front at the opening

explanation.definitionFit: In chess these eight pieces start on the row ahead of the major pieces.

clue.text: Sympathetic about egghead member of the family

indicators.note: one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a nice person is kind and sympathetic
the head of egg is its first letter

explanation.surface: A kindly intellectual relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egghead' suggests an intellectual but gives just the first letter of egg.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a sibling's daughter, a relative.

clue.text: Lady dines out, showing gluttony perhaps?

indicators.note: the letters come out of order, rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman eating at a restaurant overindulges.
explanation.definitionFit: Gluttony is one of the seven traditional cardinal vices, so an example.

clue.text: By which we are well refreshed

definitions.text: By which we are well refreshed

parts.words: By which we are well refreshed
parts.note: 'well' looks like an adverb, but is the water source we drink from

explanation.definitionFit: Natural water from a spring or well is drunk to refresh people.
